parallel.requirements: Recognized the same Rust 2021, CLI argument gates, exact numeric/output formatting, zero-dependency, module organization, and black-box executable-probing requirements from the prompt.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Although swarm mode was enabled, no child owner was created; the main agent retained ownership for probing, implementation, fixes, verification, and final delivery.
parallel.implementation: Implemented a Cargo project with /output/test13.rs and color modules, using f32 hue difference with a single fold and custom formatting plus custom std::stof-like parsing/error behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The main agent wrote all package files into /output, compiled both rustc and Cargo release outputs, and left the expected entry file and executable artifacts for evaluation.
parallel.verification: It probed the reference executable, ran build checks, caught two differential mismatches around stof underflow/zero mantissa handling, edited the parser, then passed a broad final sweep.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unresolved implementation issue is evidenced at closure; official evaluation passed all 40 testcases and the final response reports successful differential testing.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same prompt requirements for a pure Rust 2021 Cargo project, root test13.rs, exact CLI defaults, and byte-for-byte numeric output matching.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single serial main agent owned the complete path: executable probing, implementation, package layout, building, differential verification, and final response.
serial.implementation: Implemented a Cargo project with colorspace modules, f32 hue-difference logic using a single conditional fold, C++-style float formatting, and Rust parse().expect for CLI floats.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial run wrote all files into /output, built the Cargo release binary and a rustc standalone check, and delivered the expected root test13.rs plus modules.
serial.verification: It probed the reference executable, confirmed edge behavior, built with Cargo and rustc, then ran documented, default, edge, and 400+ randomized differential cases with ALL MATCH.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official failure is evidenced. Compared to the parallel solution, invalid/prefix/underflow std::stof edge behavior was less fully emulated, but the evaluator still passed it.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received and acted on the Rust 2021, same CLI, exact output, zero dependency, /output Cargo project, and black-box probing requirements.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received the same prompt and similarly identified the required Rust project, CLI gates, exact hue behavior, and output formatting constraints.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-coverage difference for official acceptance; parallel went further on std::stof failure semantics while serial relied on valid-float parsing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel mode was enabled, but the main agent explicitly kept the small task direct and no subagents were created or delegated to.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used the expected single main-agent control path with no swarm mode and no subagent activity.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The only decomposition difference is that parallel had swarm mode available but unused; both actual solution attempts were single-owner main-agent workflows.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: There were no child briefs, child handoffs, cross-agent contracts, or parent-child context transfers because no delegation occurred.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were also no handoffs or inter-agent interfaces in the serial run; all context remained in the main agent's trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No coordination-context difference exists; both depended on local probing and local implementation rather than cross-agent interfaces.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote color modules plus custom stof and cformat modules, then fixed underflow and zero-mantissa parsing after differential-test failures.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote colorspace modules with hue-difference and formatting logic, but used Rust parse().expect rather than a custom std::stof emulation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented the accepted hue algorithm and formatting; parallel's implementation was more exhaustive around stof edge cases, while serial was simpler but officially sufficient.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All work remained in the main trajectory; after the final successful sweep, the main agent summarized the finished artifacts and no child result was pending.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial likewise closed from the main trajectory after successful verification and final artifact summary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No result lifecycle coordination issue exists; there were no delegated results to retrieve, inspect, merge, or abandon in either run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced a coherent /output artifact set with Cargo.toml, test13.rs, color modules, and release build artifacts listed by validation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced a coherent /output artifact set with Cargo.toml, test13.rs, colorspace modules, and release build artifacts listed by validation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both integrated their own files without concurrent write conflicts; directory names differed but each final tree was internally consistent and accepted.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel compiled with rustc and Cargo, ran differential checks, corrected failures, then recorded ALL TESTS PASSED before the official 40/40 evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial built with Cargo and rustc and ran documented, edge, default, and randomized differential tests, recording ALL MATCH before the official 40/40 evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had strong black-box verification; parallel used failures to drive two parser fixes, while serial's simpler implementation passed its differential suite immediately.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed without timeout after one provider attempt, but spent more time and tokens while handling extra parser edge cases.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed without timeout after one provider attempt with fewer seconds, fewer requests, and fewer tokens.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel was more expensive but not budget-constrained; both closed cleanly with successful evaluations and no unfinished child or timeout chain.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current official status.json evaluation records both solutions as completed and passed 40/40, so the relation is both_pass. The practical task-solving difference is that the parallel-mode run did not actually parallelize; it solved directly and added stricter std::stof-compatible edge handling after test mismatches. The serial run also solved directly and passed with a simpler parse-based CLI implementation. Because both artifacts satisfied the official evaluator, there is no discordant outcome to explain and no parallel coordination episode with an adverse realized consequence.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel implemented custom std::stof-like prefix, overflow, and underflow behavior after observing differential failures.
Serial used Rust parse().expect for CLI floats, which is simpler and potentially differs on invalid, prefix, or ERANGE inputs but still passed official tests.
Parallel used /output/color modules while serial used /output/colorspace modules; both layouts were internally consistent Cargo projects.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; implementation differences are ordinary and not tied to parallel coordination
